act1.text: Act I · Sitting down at the machine

act3.text: Kit · Platinum Indigo, vector chrome from 1080p to 4K

c1.text: Beat 1. A Q8B boots to this in under 3 s. Workspace 1 is `space`: Tracker's home folder reopens where it was left (frame stored as a Taisce attribute). The Terminal has the focused yellow tab; it has just mounted the Q8B over 9gate. Deskbar sits top-right with live gauges and a 2×2 workspace grid marked S/T.

c2.text: Beat 2. One chord or a click on the workspace's S/T chip projects the same windows into master-stack. The mode bezel confirms it and fades. Tabs fold into strips; nothing is lost: flipping back restores every spatial frame. Budget: done within 2 frames of input.

c3.text: Beat 3. A query is a folder. Built in the Find pane's MUI-style group, it stays live: the count ticks as the camera ring on the Q8B lands frames on disk. Columns are attributes. Get Info shows typed attributes and provenance (sys:origin-app).

c4.text: Beat 4. The Inspector is principle 19 made visible: jobs and processes, threads with their declared intent (never a priority), what each waits on (always a port), its handles, the rings it shares with their cursors, and the budgets with their limits.

c5.text: Beat 5. The NeXT browser walks the namespace across machines: /n/q8b/dev/accel/cdsp0 is a directory with .help, .schema, ctl and ring. The patch bay draws what the control plane negotiated: camera ring → remote CDSP → the game's render ring. The CPU never touches the frames.

c6.text: Beat 6. Appearance sets one UI scale from 100% to 300%; chrome is vector, so 4K is a number, not a second set of bitmaps. A recorder asks for `capture`: the keyring's prompt is a trusted surface, dimming everything, deaf to injected input and blacked out in captures.
